do_more: Lean into 'The Confidence Curve' energy: use titles that promise a specific, relatable psychological shift rather than a generic concept.
Use concrete, slightly absurd physical objects or scenarios (like a jacket or a clean room) as the visual anchor for the psychological idea.
Keep the average watch time high (aim for >50% retention) by ensuring the first 3 seconds show a distinct, funny visual action, not just a title card.
avoid: Do not use the word 'Trap' or 'Spiral' in titles; this pattern correlates with the lowest performance and was explicitly rejected by the owner.
Avoid abstract, high-level academic concepts without a immediate, tangible visual gag (e.g., 'The IKEA Effect' underperformed compared to 'The Jacket He Never Wears').
Do not repeat the 'Leo & Mia #X' numbering in titles; the top performers did not use this format.
short.title_style: Use 'The [Specific Object/Situation] [Noun]' structure that implies a hidden behavioral quirk, avoiding generic psychology terms.
next_tests: Test a 'Redundancy' hook: Start the video with Leo saying something obvious, then Mia physically demonstrates why it's wrong (visual-first).
Test a 'Time-Lapse' angle: Show Leo trying to do a simple task (like tying shoes) but the animation slows down to show the internal panic/confidence curve in real-time.
